name: Southern Rengma Naga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Kumar, Braj Bihari. 1973. Rengma vyakaran ki ruparekha [Outline of Rengma grammar]; Marrison 1967 Naga classification PhD

new_statements.quote: Tonemes show a three-way contrast in the Terüpvunyu and Tseminyu dialects of Rengma. That said, the illustrations provided are from the dialect that interests us here. Three level tones – low [˨], mid [˧], and high [˦] – occur in open syllables, including those containing nasalised vowels. [...] The same tonemes also appear in syllables that end in nasals. [...] Low tone is perceived in syllables ending in /t/, while syllables with a glottal stop in the coda position can carry a low or a high tone. [p.11:] It can be sequenced as (C1)(L)V(C2)T, with C1(L) as the onset [...] V is the obligatory nucleus, C2 is the optional coda, and T is the tone on the syllable.
new_statements.citation: Debnath, Rupak. 2023. A Phonological description of Nzang Terüpvunyu khwen (Assam Rengma). Unpublished manuscript, archive.org (item assam-rengma-phonological-description), 18 July 2023.
new_statements.locator: §5.2 Suprasegmental phonology, p. 10; syllable template §6.1, p. 11
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (extracted text of the saved PDF; pdfinfo: 31 pages, created 21 Jul 2023 — the report's 'c. 40 pp.' is a small overcount, otherwise the citation matches the title block: 'A Phonological description of Nzang Terüpvunyu khwen (Assam Rengma)', Rupak Debnath, unpublished manuscript, created 18-07-2023, archive.org 15-08-2023). The quoted passage is there verbatim: '5.2 Suprasegmental phonology / Tonemes show a three-way contrast in the Terüpvunyu and Tseminyu dialects of Rengma. That said, the illustrations provided are from the dialect that interests us here. Three level tones – low [˨], mid [˧], and high [˦] – occur in open syllables, including those containing nasalised vowels.' (line…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Rengma is a tone language: every syllable carries one of three level tonemes (low, mid, high), contrastive in open, nasal-final and glottal-checked syllables; pronominal prefixes copy the root tone, other prefixes (a-, n-, ke-) carry a stable low tone. The description contains no statement about word stress or accent at all (neither a placement rule nor a denial), so no stress position can be read off it.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone: /t/-final syllables only low; glottal-final low or high; prefix allotony as above. Nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word/syllable level; examples are isolated words and short phrases with tone letters; the author says the three-way tone contrast holds in both the Terüpvunyu (Assam) and Tseminyu (Nagaland) dialects. Older sources agree it is tonal but give no stress information: Mills 1937:287 ('tones have only been noted where of special importance. Only syllables which are very strongly long or short have been so marked'); Grierson 1903:237 ('distinguished by being pronounced with different tones, but no information is available on this point'); Longmailai 2019:2 ('Rengma is a tonal language... phonology... yet to be completed').
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted phonology (Debnath 2023) describes Nzang Terüpvunyu khwen, the Western/Assam (Karbi Anglong) dialect of Rengma proper (Mills' 'Rengma A'); Glottolog lists 'Western Rengma' and 'Terüpvunyu' among the alternate names of sout2732, and the author states that the three-way tone contrast holds in both the Terüpvunyu and the Tseminyu (Nagaland) dialects. It is not Northern Rengma / Ntenyi (nort2725, nnl), which Mills and Debnath treat as a distinct language ('Rengma B'). Longmailai 2019 and the Baruah papers likewise describe Western Rengma.

sources.note: Full phonology of the Western/Assam (Terüpvunyu) dialect; §5.2 'Suprasegmental phonology' (p.10) treats only tone: three level tonemes (low, mid, high) in open, nasal-final and checked syllables; syllable = (C1)(L)V(C2)T with T the tone (p.11). The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the paper (grep: 0 hits).

sources.note: No descriptive references beyond Longmailai 2019 for sout2732; nort2725 lists none. Alternative names for sout2732 include 'Western Rengma', 'Nzong', 'Nzonyu', 'Terüpvunyu', 'Unza', 'Injang' - confirming the Assam dialect described by Debnath belongs under this glottocode.
